Subject: Clarify billing cadence for HIPAA evidence + residency KMS seat

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team appreciated the latency numbers and the residency options. Procurement asked us to get a single-line summary on how you intend to bill the compliance/security add-ons so we can proceed. Two specific asks: 

1) HIPAA evidence delivery (SOC-like evidence, policy docs, attestation): is the evidence/evidence-delivery fee a one-time implementation charge or a recurring line item? If recurring, what cadence and what unit (per-seat, per-region, fixed-monthly)?

2) Residency + KMS/HSM: we need clarity on the billing split for the KMS/HSM seat versus throughput (per-token or capacity). Will the residency surcharge be monthly flat + usage, or do you offer an amortized implementation credit (spread over N months) to offset upfront integration?

I've attached our internal checklist for evidence items for reference (Medica_Evidence_Checklist.pdf). Can you provide a short pricing summary we can hand to procurement?

Best,
Asha

Head of AI Platforms, Medica Health


From: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Clarify billing cadence for HIPAA evidence + residency KMS seat

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear asks and for the checklist. Below is a concise summary you can share with procurement, plus two packaging options depending on whether Medica prefers upfront simplicity or predictable monthly economics. Attached: redwood_pricing_workback_may19.xlsx (detailed numbers).

Quick summary for procurement (one-line):
Redwood charges a one-time evidence/attestation delivery fee (covers evidence collection and initial attestations) plus a monthly residency surcharge (region + KMS/HSM seat), with optional amortization of the one-time fee into monthly credits on 12-month commitments.

Packaging options (pick one):
1) Upfront + Recurring (Default)
  - Evidence delivery: one-time implementation fee (listed in attached workback).
  - Residency & KMS: monthly residency surcharge (per-region) + monthly KMS seat fee (per-seat), usage billed separately for sustained throughput.
  - Pros: clean separation on books; no change to monthly unit billing.

2) Amortized credit (recommended for pilots / procurement-friendly contracts)
  - Evidence delivery: billed as one-time but Redwood applies an implementation credit amortized over first 12 months (reduces monthly invoice by equal credits).
  - Residency & KMS: same monthly structure but we can offer a 50% residency surcharge credit for first 3 months on a 12-month committed term.
  - Pros: smoother monthly invoices for budget approval; helps procurement accept pilot phase.

Operational notes:
- Evidence delivery timeline: typical 4–6 weeks from kickoff for the items in your checklist; longer if Medica requests custom attestation language.
- Audit log retention: retention tiers are configurable; longer retention increases storage surcharge (we list options in the workback).
- Attachments: redwood_pricing_workback_may19.xlsx includes sample amortization math and invoice phasing you can paste into your PO.

I can send a one-page summary slide for procurement if useful. If you prefer the amortized option, tell me and I’ll loop in Laura to finalize concession authority.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_pricing_workback_may19.xlsx

Asha / Ben — looping in Hannah and Dev for ops / legal impacts. Ben, thanks for the tidy options. From a commercial standpoint we can do the amortized-credit path with a pilot concession to help Medica close procurement quickly. Proposal for approval: 

Commercial offer (summary):
- Term: 12 months committed
- Pilot concession: 50% off residency surcharge for first 3 months (applied as invoice credit)
- Implementation/evidence fee: billed one-time at kickoff; Redwood will apply an implementation credit amortized across first 12 monthly invoices to smooth the P&L (credit math matches the attached workback).
- KMS/HSM: seat fees billed monthly; usage/throughput billed according to the plan in the workback.
- Audit log retention: default 90 days; additional retention billed at $X/month per TB (we'll provide exact line).

Operational ask for Dev/ops: can you confirm that the amortized credit approach is ok from an invoicing and credit-recognition perspective and whether any additional provisioning delay is expected when HSM seats are reserved?

If ops signs off, I’ll ask Legal to prepare an amendment showing the commit + concession and a DocuSign envelope for signature. We can include a single-line commercial summary for procurement to attach to the PO.

Laura Bennett
Head of Sales, Enterprise — Redwood Inference
